title: [Afterpay] Ubiquiti U7 Pro XGS Black Wireless Access Point, Wi-Fi 7, 10G Poe++ Port $497.25 Delivered @ Digilifeonline eBay
body:
Deal: [Afterpay] Ubiquiti U7 Pro XGS Black Wireless Access Point, Wi-Fi 7, 10G Poe++ Port $497.25 Delivered @ Digilifeonline eBay

[Larsson] Had nothing but trouble with my U7 Pro XG. Random connection drops where my old ASUS router/AP combo easily served, coming home to wifi connecting but not having internet until I disconnect and reconnect, stuff randomly changing in my config due to updates despite not touching anything.
I have their cloud fibre gateway too.
UniFi really sucks. Never again…
[Midday Murth] I've heard that a bit with U7 access points. Had great results with the U6 based ones.
[Haulien] I had some issues with a TP-Link AP where the switch it was being powered off had PoE++ in the specs but the port wasn't providing the required wattage causing dropouts. Ended up replacing the switch and the AP has been fine since.
I wonder if the issue you had is similar, your switch just not outputting the power required even though it's rated.
[Larsson] Almost certainly because this happened (initially) when they introduced a toggle for power management. Before then, it was actually working totally fine.
Cloud gateway fiber has Poe+ port so I expect this to work with U7 Pro XG.
But all the random breaking changes with overnight updates absolutely kills UniFi for me. It’s so unstable, and they change so much so quickly, I can’t believe people don’t complain more
[Nom] Cloud gateway fiber has Poe+ port so I expect this to work with U7 Pro XG.
No, U7 Pro needs PoE++
[Larsson] @Nom: I think UniFi might know what their devices specs are:
Power Method: PoE+
Max. Power Consumption: 22W
So this should be below 30W even when it requires peak power.
https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/wifi/u7-pro-xg
[OzComment] My 2 U7 Pro XG have been great since day 1.
[intrepidswashbucker] I had one that seemed to drop internet once a week and required physically disconnected Poe and plugging it back in
Made a bunch of settings changes with Claude’s help; esp turned off meshing, and booted IoT stuff onto their own dedicated vlan and 2.4GHz SSID, added 2 more XG’s and haven’t had any issues since
I don’t think I’ve ever had an update cause an issue, but I’m only 10 months in
[trippy] I am 5 years in with a dream machine SE and have never had anything break after an update.
[CanolaRevolver] I love my other Unifi gear but man the Pro XG really disappointed me too. As a replacement for my Aruba AP325 it’s almost worse in every way. Signal strength on the 5ghz band is far less, frequent drop outs and random issues with no internet connection.
Even with 6ghz enabled it’s only getting speeds great than 500mbps if I’m right under the AP (where I see my M5 MBP get the gigabit speed my NBN has). Based on that I’ve swapped back to my Aruba as it’s coverage is far better and I get ~500 almost everywhere in the house.
[jackv] Incorrect wireless config it may impact on stability. Tried to ask AI to review my config and significantly improved stability after changing few settings. Not an issue anymore. Quite happy with unifi atm
[opt] I’ve had a couple of U7 Pro APs running quite well for a little over two years. There have been a few dud firmware versions along the way, but if you read user comments and manually pick the right firmware with the fewest complaints, and configure them properly they can be pretty good. I recently upgraded to 8.7.11 RC, and it’s been quite stable.
[Larsson] I don’t know what you think about this overall but the experience you outlined is completely unacceptable to me.
If I auto config everything, it should just work. It does on every single other router I ever touched. It’s absolutely crazy to me UniFi is the outlier and this is acceptable to people.
As I said elsewhere though, if you manually play around, yes sure it’s hard to know if it was you or UniFi.
[voltagex] Go for the XG over the XGS.
If you don't need gigabit speeds, the U7 Lite will also work.
EnGenius worth a look but the firmware makes Ubiquiti and TP-Link Omada look good.
[yellah] I returned my XGS and got a U7 instead 💀
Wasn't happy with it's range although probably my fault for expecting more from it.
[scaryspace] Out of curiosity, where did you buy/return it to?
[Sarquiss] Well, now I’m confused. Been waiting for a deal on the XGS after hearing that it improved on the XGS. Currently have a Cloud Gateway Fibre, which has been sitting in a box waiting for a new AP (My old ASUS Wifi Router has been having issues).
Primarily looking for good coverage and speeds
[bri11iant-y] Which Asus router are you using and how many AP do you have? I'm also using ASUS routers now and tempted to get into the ubiquiti eco system becasue I have heard good words about them. I'm in a "I want them but I dont need them" situation.
Do you think spending ~900+ on their products is justifiable for your needs?
[Sarquiss] I’m actually running a Netgear Nighthawk X10 (No idea why I thought I was running a ASUS router).
I’m starting somewhat small with regards to Uniquiti gear (Already have a Cloud Gateway Fibre and will be looking to pick up a single AP - for now).
[oobadeedee] Ugh…I'm quite torn. Have been eyeing U7 Pro XG for a new build, have been advised XGS is way overkill.
But now hearing more advice that U7 is problematic as a generation compared to U6.
Now considering U6E
[trippy] I added a U7 lite in addition to my U6 Pro and it has been very stable for 6 months now. No real Wifi 7, but the wifi is just for portable devices and smart things.
